dataset.datasetnotes: This dataset was originally uploaded to the Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University constituent database, which was merged into the Diatom Paleolimnology Data Cooperative (DPDC) constituent database in July 2026.

All lakes were sampled as part of the US EPA's 2017 National Lake Assessment.

Surface sediment samples were collected by crews from individual state agencies at the time they were doing other sampling for the EPA National Lake Survey.  Samples from sediment core intervals 0-1 and 1-2 cm were both saved.  Diatom analysis was performed on the combined material from both intervals (0-2 cm).  No core material was saved for future analysis.

No data on lake or watershed characteristics were available from EPA at the time data were entered into Neotoma (November 2018).  Data are expected to be available in the future at: https://www.epa.gov/national-aquatic-resource-surveys/nla
-------

From NE Voucher flora website:https://diatoms.org/projects/northeast-lakes-regional-flora

"This project is a model for ensuring taxonomic consistency across analysts by 1) use of Battarbee Chambers, 2) randomizing sample assignment to analysts, 3) developing a pre-voucher flora, 4) coordinating analysts through weekly webinars, 5) ensuring 20% repeat counts (10% and self 10% cross QA/QC), 6) documenting taxon names and sources, and 7) thorough project documentation.

1) Sediments from 106 lakes in the northeast were processed to produce quantitative slides, through the use of Battarbee Chambers.

2) The samples, along with 6 replicate samples, were randomized for assignment to 3 analysts.

3) A pre-voucher flora based on over 4000 digital images was developed to represent the taxonomic diversity and morphologic range of species.

4) Seven weekly webinars were held for analysts to discuss problematic taxa and highlight new taxa added to the flora as they were encountered. Newly encountered taxa were imaged and incorporated into a weekly updated flora. We led a workshop with the analysts and other interested experts at the Diatom Herbarium at the Academy of Natural Sciences in Philadelphia on March 27-30, 2018 to assign species names and resolve difficult species boundaries in this project. 

5) A rigorous QA/QC procedure documents analyst self consistency and cross analyst consistency.

6, 7) The flora, taxon names, references and R scripts documenting the project and preparing the data for analysis are available at the INSTAAR link. 

Funding
US Environmental Protection Agency
Regional Voucher Flora and taxon webpages for North Eastern Lakes - Sarah Spaulding

site.sitedescription: Tsuga candensis, Fagus grandifolia, Acer saccharum, Pinus strobus, and Betula species are common in the northern, inland, and higher-elevation parts of New England. Quercus, Carya, and Castanea dentata dominate in the warmer southern part of the region. Acer rubrum is common across New England. Pinus rigida is prevalent on sites with well-drained sandy soils.

dataset.datasetnotes:
From Dixit et al 1999:
"In addition to various limnological measurements made in the field, water samples were collected for detailed chemical analysis (Baker et al. 1997). These water samples were taken from the 1.5-m water depth, or from the 0.5-m depth if the lake was <2 m deep. The details of field sampling protocols and methods used for the chemical analysis in EMAP-SW are presented in Baker et al. (1997). The EMAP-SW resource group provided all the necessary physical, chemical, and land use data for the study lakes. These data can be found on EMAP’s web site (http://www.epa.gov/emap/ html/dataI/surfwatr/data/nelakes)."

Each lake was sampled once at the same time the core was taken.

“Water chemistry samples were collected from the epilimnion using a 2 m PVC tube.  Sampling depth was 2 m unless euphotic zone (Secchi disk depth x 2) was <2m, in which case, water sampling depth was equal to the euphotic zone.  All methods are described in EPA NLA publications.  Basic measurement data were added to Neotoma; flags and tags were not.  Data and documentation are available from the EPA website https://www.epa.gov/national-aquatic-resource-surveys/data-national-aquatic-resource-surveys (as of April 2019).”
